facts.statement: Genyodectes is a genus of ceratosaurian theropod dinosaur whose name means "jaw bite" in Greek.
facts.quote: Genyodectes ("jaw bite", from the Greek words genys ("jaw") and dektes ("bite")) is a genus of ceratosaurian theropod dinosaur from the Lower Cretaceous (Aptian) of South America.

facts.statement: The holotype of Genyodectes was collected from the Cerro Barcino Formation in the Chubut Province of Argentina.
facts.quote: The holotype material (MLP 26–39, Museo de La Plata, La Plata, Argentina) was collected from the Cerro Barcino Formation, Cañadón Grande, Departamento Paso de Indios in the Chubut Province of Argentina

facts.statement: Genyodectes had relatively large and protruding premaxillary teeth similar to those of Ceratosaurus.
facts.quote: The premaxilla of Genyodectes possesses relatively large and protruding teeth, similar to those of Ceratosaurus.

facts.statement: In 2016, Genyodectes was estimated to reach a length of 6.25 meters and a weight of 790 kilograms.
facts.quote: In 2016 it was estimated to be 6.25 m in length and 790 kg in weight.

facts.statement: The genus Genyodectes was described by English paleontologist Sir Arthur S. Woodward in 1901.
facts.quote: English paleontologist Sir Arthur S. Woodward described Genyodectes in 1901

facts.statement: Genyodectes differs from most theropods by having premaxillary teeth arranged in an overlapping en-echelon pattern, a trait also found in Ceratosaurus.
facts.quote: Differs from all theropods with the possible exception of Ceratosaurus in that the premaxillary teeth are arranged in an overlapping en-echelon pattern

facts.statement: Genyodectes can be distinguished from Ceratosaurus by having four premaxillary teeth instead of three.
facts.quote: Differs from Ceratosaurus in the presence of four, as opposed to three, premaxillary teeth.

facts.statement: The taxonomic validity of Genyodectes was strengthened after the holotype was removed from the artificial matrix in which it had been displayed for a long time.
facts.quote: However, the removal of the holotype from the "artificial matrix" in which it had long been displayed has permitted a reevaluation of the specimen.

facts.statement: Research by Rauhut (2004) concluded that Genyodectes lacks key abelisaurid and tyrannosaurid traits but possesses many neoceratosaurian characteristics.
facts.quote: Rauhut (2004, p. 900) concluded that the specimen lacks important abelisaurid and tyrannosaurid synapomorphies, but found many neoceratosaurian traits.

facts.statement: Evidence suggests Genyodectes was phylogenetically closer to Ceratosaurus than to more derived abelisaurs.
facts.quote: This would seem to imply Genyodectes was closer to Ceratosaurus than the more derived abelisaurs

facts.statement: Rauhut (2004) concluded the Genyodectes holotype was likely collected from the Cerro Castaño Member of the Cerro Barcino Formation during the Aptian to Albian stages.
facts.quote: Rauhut (2004, p. 894) concluded that the specimen was likely collected from the Cerro Castaño Member of the Cerro Barcino Formation (Aptian-Albian).

facts.statement: Genyodectes lived during the middle Late Cretaceous, approximately 112 million years ago in the Albian stage, in what is now South America.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Cretácico Superior, hace 112 millones de años, durante el Albiense, en lo que hoy es Sudamérica.

facts.statement: The time range for Genyodectes is recorded as the Albian stage, between 113.2 and 100.5 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Albian (113.2 to 100.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: Over the last decade, the classification of Genyodectes has been debated, with it being referred to variously as a megalosaurid, tyrannosaurid, Theropoda incertae sedis, or a possible abelisaurid.
facts.quote: Over the last decade, the holotype has been variously referred to as a megalosaurid, a tyrannosaurid, Theropoda incertae sedis, and a possible abelisaurid

facts.statement: Some estimates suggest Genyodectes could have reached a length of around 9 meters.
facts.quote: Se ha estimado que media alrededor de 9 metros de largo.

rejected.statement: Genyodectes was the second non-avian dinosaur described from the South American continent, following Loncosaurus.
rejected.quote: after Loncosaurus (Ameghino, 1899; nomen dubium), it is the second non-avian dinosaur described from the South American continent
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'the second non-avian dinosaur described from the South'

rejected.statement: Genyodectes remained the most completely known South American theropod until the 1970s.
rejected.quote: it remained the most completely known South American theropod until the 1970s.
rejected.reason: statement copies the source wording: 'remained the most completely known South American theropod'
